title: Route-Class Uplift on Card-Paid Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements Segments
content:
On a Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements agreement, the route class of a card-paid ticket booked under the agreement adds to the card-paid uplift on each of its flown segments. The route class is the itinerary class on the ticket's record in Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.

| Route class of the card-paid ticket | Addition to the card-paid uplift |
|---|---|
| long-haul international | 20 percentage points |
| short-haul international | 10 percentage points |
| domestic | nothing |

**How the card-paid uplift acts.** The card-paid uplift is counted in percentage points; uplifts on different grounds are added together, and the segment's earned card-paid segment points are raised by the total: the points posted are the earned points multiplied by one hundred plus the card-paid uplift, divided by one hundred, rounded down to the whole point once at the end.

### Questions on the route class

**Which route class counts?** The one recorded on the card-paid ticket itself, for every flown segment of that ticket.

**What does a long-haul segment with no other uplift post? (hypothetical)** Earned points of 918 raised by 20 percentage points: 918 multiplied by 120 and divided by one hundred is 1101.6, rounded down to 1101 points.

**What does a domestic segment with no other uplift post?** Its earned points as they are.
